Crm-28594-2015 Application is allowed as prayed for subject to all just exceptions.

Main case Aggrieved of the judgment of acquittal dated 09.01.2014 passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Amritsar in case bearing FIR No.42 dated 05.03.2012, under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, registered at Police Station 'A' Division, Amritsar in Criminal case bearing No.138 dated 08.05.2012 and the subsequent dismissal of Criminal Appeal bearing No.682 of 2014 by the Additional Sessions Judge, Amritsar 1 of 8 CRR-3269-2015 (O&M)
-2- vide judgment dated 05.06.2015
, the present revision petition has been filed.

2 As per the case of the prosecution, complainant Jagdish Rai son of Gian Chand Sharma, resident of Vallah, Tehsil and District Amritsar moved a complaint to the Commissioner of Police, Amritsar, for taking action against respondent-accused Jaswant Singh stating that he had been running his business of fans opposite to Shani Mandir, Vallah.

Since the petitioner-complainant was not doing any work,
accused enticed him to become 50% partner with him.

Accused allured the complainant that the latter was only to invest money in the business and the entire work would be done by the accused Jagdish Raj vs State Of Punjab & Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183377840/

sentences.text: On the assurance given by the accused, the complainant used to make payment for the purchased goods.

A total sum of Rs.3,25,000/- was paid by the complainant to the accused, out of which the complainant received some amount from the accused and a sum of Rs.1,60,000/- remained outstanding towards the accused.
Accused failed to return said amount of Rs.1,60,000/- to the complainant and was threatening him.
3 On completion of investigation, challan against the accused was presented and copies of challan were supplied to the accused.
Charges for offence punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 were framed to which accused pleaded not guilty and he claimed trial.

4 In order to prove the charge, the prosecution examined the PW.1 Sub Inspector Kuldip Singh, Investigating Officer; PW.2 Narinder Singh; PW.3 Pritpal Singh; PW.4 Jagdish Rai, complainant/author of the FIR and PW.5 Kulwant Singh.

6 Statement of accused was recorded under Section 313 of Code of Criminal Procedure.
The entire incriminating evidence against the accused was put to him, to which he denied and stated that he had been falsely implicated.
However, he did not lead any defence evidence and closed his defence evidence.
7 After hearing learned Assistant Public Prosecutor and learned defence counsel and on going through the record, learned trial Court vide impugned judgment acquitted the respondent-accused.
8 Feeling aggrieved of the judgment of acquittal passed by the trial Court, the petitioner preferred an appeal which was also dismissed by the Addl. Sessions Judge, Amritsar.
Hence, the present revision petition.
9 Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that both the Courts have failed to appreciate the evidence available on record.
He contends that the petitioner had met with a major motor vehicle accident and he suffered 30% permanent disability.
A case was filed by him before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Amritsar and compensation was awarded to him for the permanent disability.
The respondent-accused influenced him to invest the money received by him towards compensation, in his business, by promising handsome returns.

Accordingly, the petitioner started giving money to the respondent-accused on different occasions and a total amount of Rs.3.25 lakhs approximately was withdrawn by the petitioner from his bank accounts as well as that of his wife.

He contends that the said aspects were not taken into consideration by both the Courts below and the respondent-accused has been wrongly acquitted.
10 I have heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and have gone through the judgments passed by both the Courts.

11 It is evident from a perusal of the judgment passed by the trial Court that as per the case unfolded, an amount of Rs.1,65,000/- was alleged to have been entrusted to the respondent-accused, which he had dishonestly misappropriated thereof.

It was recorded that the prosecution had failed to establish that there was a fraudulent intention of the accused at the time of entering into partnership/
business relationship amongst the parties.

Further, it is also noticed that even though the entire gist of the allegations was that the business pertaining to Electric Spare Parts was to be started, however,
there was no evidence to suggest that any such partnership business had actually come into existence.

It was also noticed that the entire case of the complainant-petitioner was based upon the receipts EX.P1 to EX.P31, however, the said receipts did not bear the signatures of either the respondent-accused or the petitioner-complainant and only the name and style of M/s Popular Electric Works was mentioned.
Hence, it could not be ascertained as to who made the payment and to whom.
Thus, finding no evidence to link the respondent-accused with receipt of the money or the existence of the partnership and/or the misappropriation of the funds, the judgment of acquittal was passed.

12 In the appeal, the contentions raised by the petitioner were also noticed by the Appellate Court in its judgment dated 05.06.2015 and it 4 of 8 CRR-3269-2015 (O&M) -5- recorded its findings as under: -
"10.
I have heard learned counsel for the appellant, Addl. Public Prosecutor for the State and the learned counsel for the respondent-accused and also gone through the record.

11. In order to prove the charge against the accused for the offence under Section 406 of the Indian Penal Code, prosecution was required to establish that accused was entrusted with Rs.3,60,000/- and accused having no claim over the aforesaid amount, intentionally misappropriated and converted the same to his own use dishonestly and fraudulently.

In order to bring home the charge under Section 420 Indian Penal Code, the prosecution was required to establish that the accused deceived the complainant and fraudulently and dishonestly induced the complainant to deliver Rs. 3,25,000.

12. PWI ASI Kuldip Singh had conducted the inquiry and has proved the enquiry report Exhibit PW1/2 and agreement Exhibit PW2/3.
13.
PW2 Narinder Kumar stated that he is running business of spare parts of fans.
He knows the complainant as well as accused, who used to come to his shop to purchase the spare parts, but the payment was being made by complainant Jagdish Raj.
In his cross examination, he failed to produce any bill book or receipt or any other document to show that he is running the business of spare parts of fans.

sentences.text: Complainant Jagdish Rai in his cross examination has admitted that no document regarding partnership of 50% was written.
He also admitted that he is having no document to show that he made any payment to the accused.
He further stated that there was civil dispute with accused regarding money 5 of 8 CRR-3269-2015 (O&M) -6- transaction.
15. There is nothing on record to show that the complainant used to make the payment on behalf of the accused.

PW2 Narinder Singh failed to produce on file any documentary evidence in order to establish the bill book and income tax returns or any other document from which it can be ascertained that he is doing business with Jagdish Rai and Jaswant Singh.
PW3 Pritpal Singh in his cross examination has stated that accused Jaswant Singh used to purchase the spare parts from him and he used to make the payment in lieu of purchased spare parts.
16. The receipts Exhibit P1 to Exhibit P31 do not bear the signatures of complainant.
There is nothing on record to show that the accused cheated the complainant in any manner and induced him to deliver him a sum of Rs.3,25,000/-.
17. There is no evidence to show that complainant had entrusted any money to the accused or accused had fraudulently induced the complainant to deliver to him a sum of Rs.3,25,000/-.
If complainant invested money into the business being carried on by the accused, even at the asking of the accused, no offence of cheating is made out.

If accused has failed to pay 50% of the profits or failed to return the amount invested by the complainant, it cannot be said that there was any dishonest or fraudulent intention on the part of the accused, who induced the complainant to invest money in his business with an intention to cheat him.
Thus, the dispute if any is of civil nature.
The findings recorded by the learned trial court are correct and there is no reason to take any different view than taken by the trial court.

18. In view of the discussion above, finding no merit in the 6 of 8 CRR-3269-2015 (O&M) -7- appeal,
same is dismissed.
Record of Trial Court be sent back.
Appeal file be consigned to the record room."
13 It is evident from a perusal of the same that the contentions advanced by the petitioner have been duly taken into consideration by both the Courts.

The entire case of the prosecution, even if taken as a gospel truth, is only with respect to the allegation that 50% of the profit which was to be generated from the business of electric Spare Parts/Works towards the amount invested by the petitioner, out of funds received towards his compensation received in the MACT case on account of disability suffered by him, has not been given and the same has been misappropriated.
The argument deserves to be ignored since firstly, it was not established that any partnership had actually been formed between the parties.
Secondly, there was also no credible evidence on record to establish that any payment was transferred by the petitioner to the said partnership.
The receipts brought on record by the petitioner do not show any delivery of the property either by the petitioner or receipt thereof by the respondent-accused.
Hence, the delivery of the property itself having not been established, there was no occasion for the misappropriation thereof.

Still apart, it was also noticed by the Courts that the existence of a dishonest intention at the time of the initiation of the relationship amongst the Jagdish Raj vs State Of Punjab & Anr on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183377840/
4 parties has also not been established since, as per the case of the petitioner, the respondent-accused had made certain payments at the initial stage, hence, there was no dishonest intention at the time of initiation of business.

sentences.text: 14 Under the given circumstances, it cannot be held that the Courts have failed to appreciate the evidence in its correct perspective.

The 7 of 8 CRR-3269-2015 (O&M) -8- position in law is well established that in a case where two views are possible on a meaningful and harmonious appreciation of the evidence, the one which favours an accused has to be given precedence.
15 I find that there is no illegality, perversity or impropriety in the judgments or in the appreciation of the evidence by both the Courts that has been adduced by the petitioner.
It cannot thus be held that the conclusions drawn by the Courts are ill-founded or not based on meaningful interpretation of the evidence adduced.
16 Finding no merit, the present revision petition is dismissed.
17 Pending misc. application(s), if any, shall also stand(s) disposed of accordingly.
